This tutorial covers the mathematics that theoretical physics relies on. It starts with sets, topology and linear algebra, moves
through real and complex analysis, differential equations, the calculus of variations, Fourier and functional analysis and
probability, and ends with differential geometry, groups and Lie theory, fibre bundles, algebraic topology and spinors.

- [Sets, relations and topology](sets-relations-topology/index.qmd): sets and maps, relations, quotients and products, topological
  spaces, compactness and connectedness, metric spaces with completeness and the contraction mapping theorem.
- [Linear algebra](linear-algebra/index.qmd): vector spaces, linear maps and duals, bilinear forms, tensor products, determinants
  and trace, eigenvalues, diagonalisation and the Jordan form, the singular value and polar decompositions.
- [Real analysis](real-analysis/index.qmd): sequences, series, continuity and the Riemann integral, calculus on $\mathbb R^n$, the
  inverse and implicit function theorems with Lagrange multipliers, multiple integrals, and vector calculus.
- [Complex analysis](complex-analysis/index.qmd): holomorphic functions, contour integration, series and residues, analytic
  continuation and special functions, and the asymptotic evaluation of integrals by steepest descent and stationary phase.
- [Differential equations](differential-equations/index.qmd): existence and uniqueness, linear systems and the matrix exponential,
  Sturm-Liouville problems, special functions, the wave, heat and Laplace equations, Green's functions, and first-order equations
  solved by characteristics.
- [Calculus of variations](calculus-of-variations/index.qmd): functionals and the Euler-Lagrange equations, constraints, the second
  variation, and eigenvalues by the Rayleigh-Ritz method.
- [Fourier analysis](fourier-analysis/index.qmd): Fourier series, the Fourier transform, distributions, harmonic analysis on the
  sphere, and the Laplace transform.
- [Hilbert spaces and operators](hilbert-spaces-operators/index.qmd): Banach and Hilbert spaces, the four principles of functional
  analysis, weak topologies, bounded, compact, Fredholm and unbounded operators, spectral theory, Sobolev spaces, heat kernels and
  zeta determinants, and Banach and C\*-algebras.
- [Probability](probability/index.qmd): probability spaces, random variables and distributions, the limit theorems, and statistical
  estimation.
- [Differential geometry](differential-geometry/index.qmd): manifolds and submanifolds, forms and tensors, integration and Stokes'
  theorem, metrics and the Hodge star, connections, geodesics and curvature, surfaces, flows and Killing vectors, the Frobenius
  theorem and symplectic forms.
- [Group theory](group-theory/index.qmd): groups, cosets and homomorphisms, representations and Schur's lemma, characters, and the
  symmetric group with its Young diagrams.
- [Lie groups and algebras](lie-groups-algebras/index.qmd): Lie groups and algebras, the exponential map, Maurer-Cartan forms,
  representations, weights and roots of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, branching rules, Casimirs and the Dynkin index,
  Dynkin diagrams, Young tableaux for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, harmonic analysis on compact groups, and the Lorentz and Poincaré groups.
- [Homogeneous spaces and bundles](homogeneous-spaces-bundles/index.qmd): coset spaces, reductive decompositions and coset vielbeins,
  fibre, vector, principal and associated bundles, connections and holonomy, and the Hopf fibration.
- [Homotopy and cohomology](homotopy-cohomology/index.qmd): the fundamental group and covering spaces, higher homotopy groups and
  fibrations, de Rham cohomology, and characteristic classes.
- [Spinors and the Dirac operator](spinors-dirac-operator/index.qmd): Clifford algebras, gamma matrices, charge conjugation and
  reality conditions, spin groups, Dirac and Weyl spinors, spin structures, the Dirac operator on flat spaces, spheres and compact
  spaces, index theorems, and the chirality problem.

Each chapter sets out definitions and results, works through examples, and gives exercises to try. Every definition and theorem is
followed by ten examples and ten exercises, and each exercise has two solutions: a proof by hand and a check in SageMath. It's the
first of three connected tutorials. [Fundamentals of Theoretical Physics](../fundamentals-of-theoretical-physics/index.qmd) builds on it, and both lead to
[Kaluza-Klein Theories](../kaluza-klein-theories/index.qmd).

::: {.start-reading}
The chapters are listed in reading order in the sidebar, followed by the [glossary](glossary/index.qmd). [Start with the notation →](notation/index.qmd)
:::

## Software for symbolic computation

Symbolic computation simplifies complex equations and helps solve problems in various fields. Python and open-source tools
like SageMath make it easier to work on quantum field theory, general relativity, and beyond. The chapters use SageMath for
their worked computations.

Main libraries:

- [SageMath](https://www.sagemath.org): a comprehensive system for algebra, calculus, and numerical analysis. It's widely used
  for symbolic computation in physics.
- [Cadabra](https://cadabra.science/index.html): a tool for tensor calculations, especially in general relativity. It
  simplifies complex tensor equations.
- [EinsteinPy](https://docs.einsteinpy.org/en/latest/user_guide.html): a Python library for general relativity, with tools to
  work with Einstein's equations and relativistic phenomena.

Other libraries:

- [PyRate](https://github.com/LSartore/pyrate): a Python library for the computation of renormalization group equations for
  general, non-supersymmetric gauge theories.
- [munuSSM](https://gitlab.com/thomas.biekoetter/munussm): a Python package for studying the phenomenology of the
  μ-from-ν Supersymmetric Standard Model (μνSSM).
- [Wilson](https://wilson-eft.github.io/): a framework for effective field theory calculations in lattice gauge theory.
- [Flavio](https://flav-io.github.io/): a Python library focused on flavor physics, studying mesons and baryons.
- [TorchPhysics](https://boschresearch.github.io/torchphysics/index.html): a Python library of deep learning methods for
  solving differential equations.
- [PyFeyn](https://pyfeyn2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html): a Python library for generating and visualizing Feynman
  diagrams, used in quantum field theory.
